credit_ratings.summary: Fitch assigned a first-time Long-Term IDR of BB- with Stable Outlook; secured notes BB+/RR2 and unsecured notes BB-/RR4.
S&P affirmed the BB- issuer credit rating with Positive Outlook; upgraded existing senior secured debt to BB with recovery rating 2, and affirmed senior unsecured debt at B with recovery rating 6.

debt_events.summary: Carvana entered into and fully drew a $1.66 billion senior secured Term Loan B maturing 2033, using proceeds plus cash on hand to redeem its $1.66 billion 2030 Senior Secured Notes. The Term Loan B has no financial maintenance covenants.

Carvana reported increasing Ally's finance-receivable purchase commitment to up to $8 billion through July 2027, upsizing and extending one definitive loan-purchase agreement by $500 million through January 2028, and extending one short-term revolving facility through August 2027.
One finance-receivable revolving facility was further amended to extend its maturity to October 15, 2027.
Carvana stated it was in compliance with all debt covenants as of September 30, 2026.
Fitch notes that Carvana completed a distressed debt exchange in 2023; this is historical context, not a current default filing.

payment_behaviour.summary: Connecticut's Attorney General announced a $1.5 million settlement following hundreds of consumer complaints, including delayed payments to sellers and loan payoffs, extended title/registration delays, and inaccurate vehicle representations. The settlement included a $1 million consumer restitution fund and a state penalty.

distress_signals.summary: S&P noted staffing turnover at some reconditioning sites and higher vehicle depreciation in Q4 2025, while warning that efficiency and disciplined cost control would be critical as Carvana grows rapidly.

ownership.value: Publicly listed NYSE company; founder-led and controlled by the Garcia family. Carvana's 2026 proxy reported that, as of 2026-03-10, Ernest C. Garcia II held 56% of Class B and 50% of voting power, while Ernest C. Garcia III held 36% of Class B and 33% of voting power; Garcia Parties' Class B shares carried ten votes per share while the stated ownership threshold was met. Fitch later described Garcia II and III as controlling around 83% of voting rights. No change of control was verified in the sources opened.
ownership.as_of: 2026-07-30 (Fitch control statement; proxy ownership table as of 2026-03-10)

output.risk_rationale: Carvana's near-term debt-paying capacity has improved: Q3 2026 revenue was $8.04 billion, GAAP operating income was $714 million, adjusted EBITDA was $800 million, cash was $3.049 billion, and gross debt was $5.161 billion; Fitch also described $4.55 billion of liquidity as of March 31, 2026. Offsetting risks are speculative-grade ratings (Fitch BB-/Stable; S&P BB-/Positive), material dependence on continued receivable monetization, concentrated Garcia-family control, a historical distressed debt exchange, and documented payment/title complaints; therefore the risk is moderate rather than low.
